claim: In budding yeast, the decision of cell cycle commitment (Start) is determined by the time integration of its triggering signal Cln3.
source: In this study, we show that in budding yeast, the decision of cell cycle commitment (Start) is determined by the time integration of its triggering signal Cln3.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript showing the inverse proportional relationship between G1 length and Cln3 concentration.

claim: Whi5 is the integrator of Cln3-Cdk1 activity.
source: We further identify the Start repressor, Whi5, as the integrator.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by mathematical modeling and experimental perturbations showing Whi5 accumulates phosphorylation over time.

claim: The instantaneous kinase activity of Cln3-Cdk1 is recorded over time on the phosphorylated Whi5.
source: The instantaneous kinase activity of Cln3-Cdk1 is recorded over time on the phosphorylated Whi5, and the decision is made only when phosphorylated Whi5 reaches a threshold.
evidence: This is supported by the mathematical model and experimental data showing Whi5 phosphorylation accumulates with Cln3-Cdk1 activity.

claim: Cells adjust the threshold by modulating Whi5 concentration in different nutrient conditions to coordinate growth and division.
source: Cells adjust the threshold by modulating Whi5 concentration in different nutrient conditions to coordinate growth and division.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing Whi5 concentration increases in poor nutrient conditions (Figure 4).

claim: Signal integration strategy reduces noise and minimizes uncertainty in decision making.
source: Our work shows that the strategy of signal integration, which was previously found in decision-making behaviors of animals, is adopted at the cellular level to reduce noise and minimize uncertainty.
evidence: Supported by stochastic simulations showing the Integration Model produces lower variability in G1 length compared to the Instantaneous Model (Figure 2).

claim: Start is a major cell cycle checkpoint in budding yeast corresponding to the restriction point in mammalian cells.
source: Start is a major cell cycle checkpoint in budding yeast (corresponding to the restriction point in mammalian cells), which decides whether or not the cell should make the irreversible commitment to the next round of division (Hartwell et al., 1974).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Hartwell et al., 1974.

claim: Cln3 triggers the Start transition by activating a downstream positive feedback loop composed of the repressor Whi5, the transcription factor SBF/MBF and the cyclin Cln1/2.
source: As a G1 cyclin, Cln3 triggers the Start transition by activating a downstream positive feedback loop composed of the repressor Whi5, the transcription factor SBF/MBF and the cyclin Cln1/2 (Skotheim et al., 2008; Charvin et al., 2010) (Figure 1A upper panel).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies (Skotheim et al., 2008; Charvin et al., 2010) and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: CLN3 mRNA has a half-life of a few minutes.
source: Furthermore, both the CLN3 mRNA and the Cln3 protein turn over very fast (with a few minutes half-lives [Cross and Blake, 1993; Tyers et al., 1992; Yaglom et al., 1995])
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Cross and Blake, 1993; Tyers et al., 1992; Yaglom et al., 1995).

claim: Cln3 protein has a half-life of a few minutes.
source: Furthermore, both the CLN3 mRNA and the Cln3 protein turn over very fast (with a few minutes half-lives [Cross and Blake, 1993; Tyers et al., 1992; Yaglom et al., 1995])
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (Cross and Blake, 1993; Tyers et al., 1992; Yaglom et al., 1995).

claim: Cln3 abundance is very low with a few copies of mRNA.
source: at very low abundance (a few copies of the mRNA [McInerny et al., 1997; Arava et al., 2003] and 100–200 copies of the protein [Tyers et al., 1993])
evidence: This is cited from previous studies (McInerny et al., 1997; Arava et al., 2003; Tyers et al., 1993).

claim: Cln3 protein abundance is 100-200 copies per cell.
source: at very low abundance (a few copies of the mRNA [McInerny et al., 1997; Arava et al., 2003] and 100–200 copies of the protein [Tyers et al., 1993])
evidence: This is cited from Tyers et al., 1993.

claim: G1 length is prolonged as IPTG concentration decreases in both mother and daughter cells.
source: We found that in both mother and daughter cells G1 length is prolonged as IPTG concentration decreases, which is consistent with the previous findings that increased Cln3 dosage shortens G1 length (Di Talia et al., 2007) and suggests a negative correlation between G1 length and Cln3 level (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly observed experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Increased Cln3 dosage shortens G1 length.
source: which is consistent with the previous findings that increased Cln3 dosage shortens G1 length (Di Talia et al., 2007)
evidence: This is cited from Di Talia et al., 2007.

claim: Under full induction, the nuclear concentration of GFP-GFP-Cln3* is positively correlated with birth size.
source: Interestingly, we found that under full induction, the nuclear concentration of GFP-GFP-Cln3* is positively correlated and G1 length is negatively correlated with birth size (Figure 1—figure supplement 5), which implies that size control is maintained with the mutant Cln3 (Di Talia et al., 2007).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Under full induction, G1 length is negatively correlated with birth size.
source: Interestingly, we found that under full induction, the nuclear concentration of GFP-GFP-Cln3* is positively correlated and G1 length is negatively correlated with birth size (Figure 1—figure supplement 5), which implies that size control is maintained with the mutant Cln3 (Di Talia et al., 2007).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: G1 length is inversely proportional to the average Cln3 concentration in G1.
source: Thus G1 length is inversely proportional to the average Cln3 concentration in G1
evidence: This is derived from the linear fit in Figure 1J with slope very close to -1 (R2 = 0.91).

claim: The slope of the linear fit of log(TG1 − T0) against log(<Cln3> − Cln3c) is very close to −1 with R2 = 0.91.
source: The slope of the linear fit is very close to −1 (R2 = 0.91) (Figure 1J and Figure 1—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is the result of data analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The Integration Model leads to much smaller variability in G1 length compared to the Instantaneous Model.
source: In contrast, since the G1 length in the Integration Model depends on the integration of Cln3 level within a time window, a considerable amount of noise is averaged out. As a result, the variability in G1 length is much smaller (Figure 2A–C) and is consistent with the experimental data (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is shown by stochastic simulation results in Figure 2.

claim: The Instantaneous Model leads to a G1 length distribution with a long tail.
source: While the Instantaneous Model leads to a G1 length distribution with a long tail; this means that a significant fraction of the cells would have prolonged G1 lengths, which could be disadvantageous for the population.
evidence: This is observed in the simulation results shown in Figure 2.

claim: In near 80% of cells, the timing of Cln3 peak is different from the timing of Start.
source: However, we found that in near 80% cells, the timing of Cln3 peak is different from the timing of Start (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: It is very unlikely that Start is triggered by the instantaneous Cln3 concentration.
source: Thus, it is very unlikely that Start is triggered by the instantaneous Cln3 concentration.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that in 80% of cells, the timing of Cln3 peak differs from the timing of Start.

claim: The average half time of Whi5 nuclear entry is 13.7 min in mother cells.
source: The average half time of Whi5 nuclear entry, which is an estimate of the memory length in the mathematical model (Supplementary file 1A), is 13.7 min in mother cells and 10.6 min in daughter cells, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The average half time of Whi5 nuclear entry is 10.6 min in daughter cells.
source: The average half time of Whi5 nuclear entry, which is an estimate of the memory length in the mathematical model (Supplementary file 1A), is 13.7 min in mother cells and 10.6 min in daughter cells, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The memory length is comparable to the average G1 length from cytokinesis to Start in daughter cells in SD medium, which is 13.6 min.
source: Note that this memory length is comparable to the average G1 length (from cytokinesis to Start) in daughter cells in SD medium, which is 13.6 min in our experiment.
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental measurements.

claim: In whi5Δ strain, most cells pass Start with minimal G1 length.
source: Indeed, our experiment shows that in whi5Δ strain, most cells pass Start with minimal G1 length (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Whi5 overexpression significantly increased the percentage of cells in G1 phase.
source: The prediction is consistent with the previous finding that Whi5 overexpression significantly increased the percentage of the cells in G1 phase (Costanzo et al., 2004).
evidence: This is cited from Costanzo et al., 2004.

claim: There is a positive correlation between the integration threshold A and Whi5 concentration at the single-cell level with Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.53.
source: Remarkably, the positive correlation between A and Whi5 concentration can also be seen at the single-cell level (Pearson correlation coefficient = 0.53, Figure 3C).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Overexpressing CDC14 affects the nuclear accumulation of Whi5 and increases the percentage of cells in G1 phase.
source: It is known that overexpressing the phosphatase CDC14 affects the nuclear accumulation of Whi5 and increases the percentage of the cells in G1 phase (Visintin et al., 1998; Stevenson et al., 2001).
evidence: This is cited from Visintin et al., 1998 and Stevenson et al., 2001.

claim: The expression level of Cln2 is about three times higher than Cln1.
source: This is consistent with the fact that the expression level of Cln2 is about three times higher than Cln1 and with the previous finding that Cln2 is more potent in the Start transition (Huh et al., 2003; Tyers and Futcher, 1993; Tyers et al., 1993).
evidence: This is cited from Huh et al., 2003; Tyers and Futcher, 1993; Tyers et al., 1993.

claim: Cln2 is more potent than Cln1 in the Start transition.
source: This is consistent with the fact that the expression level of Cln2 is about three times higher than Cln1 and with the previous finding that Cln2 is more potent in the Start transition (Huh et al., 2003; Tyers and Futcher, 1993; Tyers et al., 1993).
evidence: This is cited from Huh et al., 2003; Tyers and Futcher, 1993; Tyers et al., 1993.

claim: In wild-type cells, Bck2 acts as a bypass Start trigger to prevent a too long G1 phase when Cln3 concentration is too low.
source: The result suggests that in wild-type cells, Bck2 acts as a bypass Start trigger to prevent a too long G1 phase when Cln3 concentration is too low.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that in BCK2+ strain, G1 length stops increasing at low Cln3 concentration (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).

claim: In suboptimal nutrient conditions, the Cln3-TG1 correlations shift towards right with higher Whi5tot intensity and A.
source: Indeed, we found that in suboptimal nutrient conditions, the Cln3-TG1 correlations shift towards right with higher Whi5tot intensity and A (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Whi5tot increases as growth rate decreases in both mother and daughter cells.
source: Surprisingly, Whi5tot increases as growth rate decreases and G1 length is accordingly prolonged in both mother and daughter cells (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: In poor nutrient conditions, the Start threshold is higher rather than lower.
source: It means that in poor nutrient conditions, the Start threshold is actually higher rather than lower as proposed by previous studies (Jorgensen and Tyers, 2004; Schneider et al., 2004; Turner et al., 2012), although the cell size may appear to be smaller.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Whi5tot increases in poor nutrient conditions, which increases the integration threshold A.

claim: When cells were switched from low glucose to high glucose medium, both Whi5tot intensity and G1 length decreased gradually and reached the same level as in constant high glucose medium after several cell cycles.
source: When the cells were switched from low glucose to high glucose medium, both Whi5tot intensity and G1 length decreased gradually and reached the same level as in constant high glucose medium after several cell cycles (Figure 4—figure supplement 6A–C,F,G).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: When cells were switched from high glucose to low glucose medium, Whi5tot increased fast and underwent an overshoot before it reached a steady level.
source: Contrarily, when cells were switched from high glucose to low glucose medium, Whi5tot increased fast and underwent an overshoot before it reached a steady level (Figure 4—figure supplement 6D,H).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6D,H.

claim: G1 length increased even faster than Whi5tot and its overshoot was more pronounced when cells were switched from high to low glucose.
source: G1 length increased even faster and its overshoot was also more pronounced than Whi5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 6D,I).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6D,I.

claim: When switched from high to low glucose, if the cell had not started budding, G1 phase could reinitiate.
source: Surprisingly, we found when switched from high to low glucose, if the cell had not started budding, G1 phase could reinitiate (Figure 4—figure supplement 6E).
evidence: This is experimental observation shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 6E.

claim: Signal integration has been seen in decision-making behaviors of animals.
source: Signal integration has been seen in decision-making behaviors of animals (Bowman et al., 2012; Bogacz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is cited from Bowman et al., 2012 and Bogacz et al., 2006.

claim: Daughter cells always have higher Whi5tot intensity than mother cells.
source: We also found that daughter cells always have higher Whi5tot intensity and steeper slope between Whi5tot and G1 length than mother cells (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claim: Daughter cells have steeper slope between Whi5tot and G1 length than mother cells.
source: We also found that daughter cells always have higher Whi5tot intensity and steeper slope between Whi5tot and G1 length than mother cells (Figure 4D,E).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claim: Whi5 is required for the different behaviors of mother and daughter cells under low metal stress.
source: It is also consistent with the previous finding that Whi5 is required for the different behaviors of mother and daughter cells under low metal stress (Avraham et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from Avraham et al., 2013.

claim: Cln3 responds to external and internal cues rapidly.
source: Although Cln3 and Whi5 determine G1 length together, they have very different response time. While Cln3 responds to external and internal cues rapidly, Whi5 adjusts in a much longer time scale and reinforces the change of G1 length (Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing different adaptation kinetics in Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: Whi5 adjusts in a much longer time scale than Cln3 and reinforces the change of G1 length.
source: Although Cln3 and Whi5 determine G1 length together, they have very different response time. While Cln3 responds to external and internal cues rapidly, Whi5 adjusts in a much longer time scale and reinforces the change of G1 length (Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing different adaptation kinetics in Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: The Start checkpoint coordinates cell growth and cell division.
source: The Start checkpoint coordinates cell growth and cell division and is thought to control the cell size under different growth conditions (Johnston et al., 1977; Jorgensen and Tyers, 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from Johnston et al., 1977 and Jorgensen and Tyers, 2004.

claim: Cln3 concentration in the nucleus increases with cell size.
source: It was proposed that Cln3 concentration in the nucleus (or total Cln3 abundance) increases with cell size and the Start transition is triggered when Cln3 level reaches a critical threshold (Chen et al., 2004; Jorgensen and Tyers, 2004).
evidence: This is a model proposed in previous studies (Chen et al., 2004; Jorgensen and Tyers, 2004).

claim: Cln3 responds to size through the upstream open reading frame (uORF) of its mRNA.
source: It was proposed that Cln3 responds to size through the upstream open reading frame (uORF) of its mRNA (Polymenis and Schmidt, 1997) and/or ER-associated proteins Whi3 and Ydj1 (Wang et al., 2004; Vergés et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism cited from Polymenis and Schmidt, 1997.

claim: Cln3 responds to size through ER-associated proteins Whi3 and Ydj1.
source: It was proposed that Cln3 responds to size through the upstream open reading frame (uORF) of its mRNA (Polymenis and Schmidt, 1997) and/or ER-associated proteins Whi3 and Ydj1 (Wang et al., 2004; Vergés et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism cited from Wang et al., 2004 and Vergés et al., 2007.

claim: Cdc14 is the major phosphatase responsible for Whi5 dephosphorylation in early G1.
source: By our definition, G1 starts from Whi5 nuclear entry, when Cdc14 is the major phosphatase that is responsible for Whi5 dephosphorylation (Taberner et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from Taberner et al., 2009.

claim: Cln3 cannot initiate the export of nuclear Whi5 until Cdc14 is inactivated at cytokinesis.
source: Cln3 cannot initiate the export of nuclear Whi5 until Cdc14 is inactivated at cytokinesis (Shou et al., 1999; Visintin et al., 1999).
evidence: This is cited from Shou et al., 1999 and Visintin et al., 1999.

claim: The environmental and internal conditions are sensed and passed to the Start signal Cln3.
source: The environmental and internal conditions are sensed and passed to the Start signal Cln3 (Gallego et al., 1997; Polymenis and Schmidt, 1997; Hall et al., 1998; Parviz et al., 1998; Menoyo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies (Gallego et al., 1997; Polymenis and Schmidt, 1997; Hall et al., 1998; Parviz et al., 1998; Menoyo et al., 2013).

claim: G1 length is defined as the time interval during which Whi5 resides in the nucleus.
source: G1 length is defined as the time interval during which Whi5 resides in the nucleus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is the operational definition used in this study, illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The fully induced Cln3 mutants do not change cell cycle behaviors such as the doubling time and cell size.
source: Since the fully induced mutants do not change cell cycle behaviors such as the doubling time and cell size, we consider them faithful replacements of wild-type CLN3 under our experimental conditions.
evidence: This is experimental observation used to validate the mutants.

claim: The MCM marker enters the nucleus 2 min prior to Whi5 and exports 5 min later than Whi5.
source: The MCM marker is an artificial marker generally reporting CDK activity. It enters the nucleus 2 min prior to and exports 5 min later than Whi5 (data not shown).
evidence: This is experimental observation mentioned in the text.

claim: The coefficient of variation (CV) of G1 length in wild-type cells is no more than 50%.
source: which is significantly larger than experimental observations for WT cells in previous and this studies (Di Talia et al., 2007; Skotheim et al., 2008; Charvin et al., 2008; Ferrezuelo et al., 2012) (CVs are no more than 50%, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a comparison with experimental data from multiple studies including this one.

claim: Bck2 triggers the Start transition in the absence of Cln3.
source: We also investigated how the correlation between Cln3 and G1 length is affected by Bck2, which triggers the Start transition in the absence of Cln3 (Wijnen, 1999).
evidence: This is cited from Wijnen, 1999.

claim: There is a linear relation between the integration threshold A and the total Whi5 concentration Whi5tot.
source: The first is that there is a linear relation between the integration threshold A and the total Whi5 concentration Whi5tot (a more detailed ODE model predicts that Cln3c will also change with Whi5tot [Supplementary file 1A]).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: Increasing the phosphatase activity k2 reduces memory length and increases Cln3c.
source: The second is that increasing the phosphatase activity k2 reduces memory length and increases Cln3c.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: Reducing Whi5c by weakening the positive feedback loop increases the integration threshold A.
source: The third is that reducing Whi5c by weakening the positive feedback loop increases the integration threshold A (the ODE model predicts that Cln3c will also change when perturbing the loop strength [Supplementary file 1A]).
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: Cln3 half-life by itself has no effect on the integration dynamics.
source: Note that Cln3 half-life by itself has no effect on the integration dynamics
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: Reducing the Cln3-Cdk1 catalytic efficiency k1 increases Cln3c and A proportionally.
source: and that reducing the Cln3-Cdk1 catalytic efficiency k1 (as in Cln3*) increases Cln3c and A proportionally, requiring an increased Cln3 concentration to pass Start.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mathematical model.

claim: The inverse proportionality between G1 length and Cln3 concentration is severely compromised in whi5Δ strain.
source: We further checked to what extent the inverse correlation holds by plotting G1 length and Cln3 intensity in log–log scale (Figure 3A). The slope of the linear fit is much larger than −1, suggesting that the inverse proportionality is severely compromised.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The inverse correlation in cln2Δ shifts more than in cln1Δ, suggesting that Cln2 contributes more to the positive feedback loop.
source: The correlation in cln2Δ shifts more than in cln1Δ, suggesting that Cln2 contributes more to the positive feedback loop.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the experimental data in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: The Start network is composed of two modules: Cln3-Cdk1 phosphorylating Whi5 as the triggering module and the positive feedback loop as the switching module.
source: The Start network is composed of two modules: Cln3-Cdk1 phosphorylating Whi5 as the triggering module and the positive feedback loop as the switching module (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a conceptual framework presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The two modules are coupled via Whi5.
source: The two modules are coupled via Whi5.
evidence: This is part of the conceptual framework of the Start network.

claim: The triggering module initiates Start by reducing Whi5 concentration in the nucleus.
source: The triggering module initiates Start by reducing Whi5 concentration in the nucleus.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic understanding of the Start network.

claim: The switching module sets a threshold for the nuclear Whi5 concentration, Whi5c, below which the switch will be flipped.
source: The switching module sets a threshold for the nuclear Whi5 concentration, Whi5c, below which the switch will be flipped.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic understanding of the Start network.

claim: G1 length is the time needed for the nuclear Whi5 concentration to drop below Whi5c.
source: Thus, G1 length is the time needed for the nuclear Whi5 concentration to drop below Whi5c.
evidence: This is inferred from the model of the Start network.

claim: The low abundance and short half-life of wild-type Cln3 make its detection in single cells extremely difficult.
source: The low abundance and short half-life of the wild-type Cln3 make its detection in single cells extremely difficult (data not shown).
evidence: This is an experimental observation mentioned in the text.

claim: The desired Cln3 mutants should have lower activity, requiring higher Cln3 concentration to pass Start.
source: Lower activity requires higher Cln3 concentration to pass Start and longer half-life allows more fluorescent proteins to mature before the tagged Cln3 is degraded, thus making the mutant Cln3 detectable in single cells.
evidence: This is the rationale for screening Cln3 mutants.

claim: The desired Cln3 mutants should have longer half-life to allow more fluorescent proteins to mature.
source: Lower activity requires higher Cln3 concentration to pass Start and longer half-life allows more fluorescent proteins to mature before the tagged Cln3 is degraded, thus making the mutant Cln3 detectable in single cells.
evidence: This is the rationale for screening Cln3 mutants.

claim: Two successful Cln3 mutants, CLN3R108A and CLN3D166A, were obtained from the screening.
source: Two successful mutants, CLN3R108A and CLN3D166A, were obtained from the screening.
evidence: This is the result of the mutant screening.

claim: The Instantaneous Model leads to a G1 variability of 92% with extrinsic noise.
source: When extrinsic noise is added in the model, the G1 variability of the Instantaneous Model is as large as 92%, which is significantly larger than experimental observations for WT cells in previous and this studies (Di Talia et al., 2007; Skotheim et al., 2008; Charvin et al., 2008; Ferrezuelo et al., 2012) (CVs are no more than 50%, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is the result of stochastic simulation shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The shape of the G1 length distribution generated by the Integration Model is more similar to experimental data than the Instantaneous Model.
source: Furthermore, the shape of the G1 length distribution generated by the Integration Model is more similar to that of the experimental data.
evidence: This is observed by comparing simulation results with experimental data in Figure 2C.

claim: After normalizing by Whi5tot, inverse correlations in both 1X and 2X WHI5 strains collapse to the same curve.
source: After normalizing by Whi5tot, inverse correlations in both 1X and 2X WHI5 strains are more converged and collapse to the same curve (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is experimental data analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: At least part of the variation in G1 length at low Cln3 concentration is due to the variance in Whi5tot concentration.
source: In Cln3-TG1 correlations, the variation of G1 is high when Cln3 concentration is low. At least part of the variation is due to the variance in Whi5tot concentration (and thus the variance in A).
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that normalizing by Whi5tot reduces variation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).

claim: There was no increase of MCM intensity in suboptimal nutrient condition.
source: However, we did not observe any increase of MCM intensity in suboptimal nutrient condition, nor any correlation between A and MCM intensity, suggesting that the nutrient regulation on Whi5 and the Whi5 regulation on A are specific.
evidence: This is experimental observation used to show specificity of Whi5 regulation.

claim: There is no correlation between A and MCM intensity.
source: However, we did not observe any increase of MCM intensity in suboptimal nutrient condition, nor any correlation between A and MCM intensity, suggesting that the nutrient regulation on Whi5 and the Whi5 regulation on A are specific.
evidence: This is experimental observation shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The nutrient regulation on Whi5 and the Whi5 regulation on A are specific.
source: However, we did not observe any increase of MCM intensity in suboptimal nutrient condition, nor any correlation between A and MCM intensity, suggesting that the nutrient regulation on Whi5 and the Whi5 regulation on A are specific.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of MCM changes in different nutrient conditions.

claim: Whi5 contributes to G1 delay in daughter cells.
source: The finding suggests that besides the daughter-specific Cln3 suppression by Ace2 (Laabs et al., 2003), Whi5 contributes to G1 delay in daughter cells as well.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that daughter cells have higher Whi5tot intensity.

claim: Ace2 suppresses Cln3 specifically in daughter cells.
source: The finding suggests that besides the daughter-specific Cln3 suppression by Ace2 (Laabs et al., 2003), Whi5 contributes to G1 delay in daughter cells as well.
evidence: This is cited from Laabs et al., 2003.

claim: The system could utilize the different response times of the sensor and the integrator to develop more complex strategies when adapting to environmental fluctuations and changes.
source: The system could utilize the different response times of the sensor and the integrator to develop more complex strategies when adapting to environmental fluctuations and changes.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional significance of having different response times.

claim: The G1 reinitiation after nutrient switch could not be explained by current knowledge of Start and must involve further changes in CDK and phosphatase activities.
source: This result could not be explained by current knowledge of Start and must involve further changes in CDK and phosphatase activities.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of G1 reinitiation.

claim: A full understanding of size control may need to take into account the combined action of Cln3 dynamics, Whi5tot concentration and the integration mechanism.
source: A full understanding of size control may need to take into account the combined action of Cln3 dynamics, Whi5tot concentration and the integration mechanism.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings of the study.

claim: Signal integration may be widely implemented in decision-making and signaling systems.
source: Our work shows that it is also adopted at the cellular level, suggesting a general strategy that may be widely implemented in decision-making and signaling systems (Li et al., 2010; Di Talia and Wieschaus, 2012; Doncic and Skotheim, 2013).
evidence: This is speculation about the generality of the signal integration strategy, with some support from cited studies.
